root_motivation: Always-on voice for a non-literate user requires a clean, single canonical microphone pipeline: PipeWire `module-echo-cancel` removes the laptop's own TTS so wake words don't retrigger; NoiseTorch-ng suppresses keyboard/fan/room noise; microWakeWord ONNX provides low-CPU, low-false-accept wake detection (the same engine HA Voice Preview Edition shipped in 2026); Silero VAD locates utterance boundaries; one daemon (`wm-audio`) fans the 16 kHz mono PCM out over a Unix socket to many consumers (STT first, more later) and publishes start/chunk/end/wake events on agorabus. Plan-agent collapsed two PRDs (audio-pipeline + wake) into this one because wake and VAD are thin consumers of the same mic stream — no extra process boundary justifies itself.
user_persona: Two programmatic consumers. Primary: `wm-stt` subscribes to `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/wintermute/mic.sock` for PCM and to agorabus topics (`wm.audio.wake | speech.start | speech.chunk | speech.end | mute | unmute`). Secondary: `wm-tts` and `wm-dialog` drive mute/unmute via `wm.tts.start|end` and `wm.dialog.mute_request|unmute_request`. The non-literate end-user never invokes wm-audio directly — she experiences only its consequences.

scope: Rust binary `wm-audio`: long-lived daemon that opens the configured PipeWire input node (env `WM_MIC_NODE`, fed through `module-echo-cancel` + optional NoiseTorch virtual source), resamples to 16 kHz mono PCM, and shares the stream via a lock-free ring buffer.

Three async tasks consuming the ring buffer: (a) UDS fanout at `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/wintermute/mic.sock` to N subscribers; (b) wake detection running microWakeWord ONNX every 80 ms on a 1280-sample window; (c) VAD running Silero VAD ONNX every 32 ms with rising-edge speech.start and 500 ms-confirmed silence speech.end.
agorabus publishes: `wm.audio.wake | speech.start | speech.chunk | speech.end | mute | unmute` with the payloads documented in PRD §2.3.
agorabus subscribes: `wm.tts.start | wm.tts.end` (gate wake detection during self-speech to mop up any AEC tail) and `wm.dialog.mute_request | wm.dialog.unmute_request` (full mic mute).
Startup-time AEC3 probe: parse `pw-cli`/module-load output, detect aec3 availability, fall back to classic webrtc-aec, log a single clear warning.
Hot-swap of wake word via `wm.audio.reload`: re-read `WM_WAKE_WORD` env, load new ONNX model, atomically swap the scorer without dropping mic capture.
non_goals: Installing the PipeWire drop-in (`~/.config/pipewire/pipewire.conf.d/99-wintermute.conf`) or the `wm-noise on|off` helper — those are the hook portion of this PRD, installed by wintermute-platform's hook phase, not the Rust crate.
Packaging the microWakeWord / Silero VAD / whisper.cpp ONNX models — separate `wm-models` AUR-style package per PRD §2.5; wm-audio loads them from `/usr/share/wintermute/models/`.
Custom-trained wake words (Fleet 3 if microWakeWord training improves).
Bluetooth audio routing and multi-mic beamforming (Fleet 2/3).
`wm-audio dump` subcommand for the rolling 10 s PCM buffer (PRD §7 says cheap to add in iter-2; defer).
Defining systemd unit files (`wm-audio.service`) — installed via wintermute-platform's hook portion.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does wintermute need a dedicated `wm-audio` daemon rather than letting each consumer (wm-stt, future diarization) open the mic directly?
five_whys_trace.a: Because PipeWire's `module-echo-cancel` only attaches cleanly to ONE capture chain at a time, and AEC is non-negotiable for always-on voice (TTS retriggering wake is the failure mode the whole fleet falls apart on). One canonical AEC'd + NS'd capture stream owned by `wm-audio`, fanned out to N consumers over UDS, also avoids N redundant ONNX wake/VAD inferences and lets the daemon gate wake-detection on `wm.tts.start`/`end` events centrally.

five_whys_trace.q: Why microWakeWord over openWakeWord, Porcupine, or Snowboy?
five_whys_trace.a: Home Assistant's Voice Preview Edition shipped microWakeWord (not openWakeWord) in 2026 precisely because the false-accept profile is better for always-on use and CPU draw is much lower. openWakeWord's custom-wake-word training pipeline has known synthetic-TTS-vs-real-voice mismatch issues, and the primary user can't retrain. Porcupine is closed-source / commercial. Snowboy is unmaintained. microWakeWord ships pretrained `hey_jarvis | okay_nabu | hey_mycroft` — pick one, let the user learn it.

five_whys_trace.q: Why Silero VAD specifically, and why a separate VAD at all (microWakeWord could in theory mark utterance boundaries)?
five_whys_trace.a: Silero VAD is the 2026 standard for turn-end detection: ONNX, ~1 MB, well-understood with documented hangover/confirmation tuning. microWakeWord fires once per utterance start at most; it cannot tell you when the user has finished speaking. End-of-speech matters for STT (you have to know when to flush the buffer and run inference) and for dialog turn-taking. The two models address different questions and the cost of both is small.

five_whys_trace.q: Why UDS fanout at `mic.sock` rather than having `wm-stt` (and future consumers) subscribe to PCM frames via agorabus?
five_whys_trace.a: agorabus is for events (small JSON payloads, sub-Hz to ~Hz publish rates). 16 kHz mono PCM at 32 ms hops is ~500 frames/s of binary data — wrong shape for a JSON bus and would dominate its throughput. A Unix-domain socket is the right primitive for the bulk-data channel; agorabus carries the metadata (wake/start/chunk-marker/end) that points at the PCM byte ranges.

five_whys_trace.q: Why detect AEC3 vs classic webrtc-aec at startup rather than just requiring AEC3 in the install docs?
five_whys_trace.a: Arch's `pipewire` package historically builds with `aec3=true` but the flag isn't guaranteed across rebuilds or Arch derivatives. A hard requirement would brick the daemon on otherwise-functional systems; a probe-and-warn keeps `wm-audio` running with classic webrtc-aec (worse but workable) and surfaces the diagnostic without requiring the operator to read pipewire build logs. Repo README documents the rebuild path for users who want AEC3.

ambiguities_resolved.question: PRD §7 open question: should NoiseTorch-ng be hard-required, or fall back to webrtc-ns (lower quality, no extra dep)?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Hard-required as documented system dep, BUT the daemon does not link or spawn it. `wm-audio` prefers the NoiseTorch virtual-source node if present at startup; falls back to `wm-mic-cancelled` (AEC-only, no NS) with a clear log line if not. PRD's leaning (hard-required) is honored in docs/install; the runtime is resilient because that's the cheaper bet.

ambiguities_resolved.question: PRD §7 open question: is there value in a `wm-audio dump` subcommand that records the last 10 s of PCM for debugging false wakes?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Deferred to iter-2. iter-1 scaffolds the single long-running daemon path only. PRD says 'probably yes; cheap to add in iter-2' and that's exactly when we'll add it — once the core pipeline is proven.

ambiguities_resolved.question: PRD §2.1 AEC3 build-flag fallback — should it be a runtime probe or a build-time feature flag?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Runtime probe at startup. The daemon parses module-load output (the `pw-cli load-module` response or `pw-dump` after configuring), sets an internal `aec_mode = Aec3 | ClassicWebrtc` flag, logs a single warning if it falls back, and continues. A build-time flag would require shipping two binaries for one laptop, which is wasteful.

ambiguities_resolved.question: PRD §2.4 defaults: what wake word ships as the out-of-box default?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: `hey_jarvis` — the most-tested microWakeWord pretrained model in 2026 HA Voice Preview Edition deployments, and the most acoustically distinct of the three (`okay_nabu` and `hey_mycroft` have closer phoneme overlap with common English words). The bootstrap form (PRD-wintermute-bootstrap AC2) lets the caregiver pick any of the three; this default applies only when WM_WAKE_WORD is unset.

ambiguities_resolved.question: PRD §2.3 `mic.sock` path — where exactly under `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/wintermute/mic.sock`. Matches the convention wintermute-platform established for `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/wintermute/init.sock`. The daemon creates the `wintermute` subdirectory at startup if absent (0700 perms, owned by the running user).

ambiguities_resolved.question: PRD §2.3 'spawn three async tasks' — tokio, smol, or hand-rolled?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: tokio (per PRD §3 dependency table). iter-1 scaffolds the layout but does NOT yet pin `tokio` in Cargo.toml; the real dependency lands in iter-2 alongside `ort`, `pipewire-rs`, `ringbuf`. iter-1's job is structure + an empty `cargo check --release`-green scaffold.
